what_it_does: Finding the k nearest points in a 3-D point cloud (for example, identifying the 10 closest sensor readings to a reference point) is a step that comes up repeatedly in self-driving car and edge-device AI pipelines. The bottleneck is usually not the math itself but the constant back-and-forth traffic between the processor and off-chip memory (large, relatively slow RAM chips). PICK is a chip design that moves the nearest-neighbor math directly into the on-chip memory (fast, small SRAM arrays) so that data barely travels at all — a technique called processing-in-memory (PIM). It uses a 'bit-serial' approach, meaning it processes numbers one binary digit at a time inside the memory array itself, which saves energy and chip space. Two additional tricks — clipping numbers to a shorter bit-width and a two-stage pipeline that overlaps distance calculation with the ranking step — further speed up the search. The result, based on the abstract, is a more energy-efficient and lower-latency kNN accelerator suited for resource-constrained settings.
